reason: Both parts reproduce exactly, driven at 1440x960 on the built master. (a) state=owner-editing: at open #b-edit-date reads '8 August 2026', .b-stepRead 'Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days', row 'Sat 8 Aug', data-away 23. After three clicks of the +7 stepper: readout 'Saturday 29 August 2026 · in 44 days', row 'Sat 29 Aug', data-away 44, data-date 2026-08-29 - and the field STILL reads '8 August 2026'. setAway() (render-b.js:550-591) writes .b-away, .b-date, the .b-grab aria-label, .b-stepRead, the stepper aria-disabled flags and the .b-ceiling hint, and never touches #b-edit-date, in direct contradiction of its own header comment claiming to be the only writer of an item's distance. Focusing the untouched field and pressing Enter fires the keydown handler at render-b.js:767 unconditionally, commitDate parses the stale '8 August 2026' and calls setAway back: measured away 44 -> 23, date 2026-08-29 -> 2026-08-08, undo bar 'Send the invitations moved 21 days earlier.' Three deliberate presses of the product's primary gesture are silently destroyed by one keystroke in the field 56px above the readout that contradicts it, with no warning and no distinct name for what was lost - the undo entry describes a move the owner never made. The behaviour gate never sees this: interaction-check.mjs:1038 and 1055 always fill() the field before pressing Enter, so it only ever commits a value the user just typed. (b) also reproduces: wireOwner captures atRest = note.textContent once at wire time (render-b.js:1026); place() rewrites .b-gapNote from live data (render-b.js:283-284); speak() restores the captured snapshot whenever the topmost visible row is rows[0]. Measured: note 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.'; move the first moment +14 to 2026-08-08 and the note correctly becomes 'Nothing is planned until 8 August.'; scroll to 900 -> '22 August · 37 days away'; scroll back to 0 -> 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' returns while the first row is data-date 2026-08-08. A sentence stating a date no moment occupies any more, repainted by scrolling, on the surface whose whole promise is that the counts cannot disagree. Same in owner-flight and owner-editing. Two write-up inaccuracies, neither load-bearing: the field and the readout are 56px apart, not 6px (the stepper row sits between them, but both are inside the one 'When' group and visible together); and blur alone does NOT revert - measured A3 leaves away at 44, because a text input's change event does not fire unless the user modified the value. Enter is the whole hazard, and it is enough. Fix is two small, correct additions and does not touch the gate at interaction-check.mjs:1901-1910, because with no edit gapSentence(rows[0].data-date) is character-identical to the captured atRest.
sharpenedFix: (a) In setAway(), immediately after computing iso, make the field the fifth consumer of the one date rather than a rival source: var when = root.querySelector('#b-edit-date'); if (when) { when.value = F.fmt.medium(iso) + ' ' + F.fmt.year(iso); when.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'false'); } - and clear the .b-ceiling refusal text with it, so a stepper press after a rejected typed date does not leave 'That is not a date' standing under a field that now reads correctly. Guard the write when the field is the active element AND its value differs from what the owner typed only if you also intend the stepper to lose - it should not: the stepper is the authority, so overwrite unconditionally. (b) In speak() (render-b.js:1029) drop the captured atRest entirely and read live from the same accessor place() uses: var rows0 = rows[0]; var said = !top || top === rows0 ? gapSentence(rows0.getAttribute('data-date')) : F.fmt.medium(...) - guarding rows.length === 0. Both writers of .b-gapNote then derive from gapSentence(), so the sentence cannot survive the fact it describes.
